artifacts.summary: Detection seam, option semantics, no-human mirror, and /approve hand-off design for offering the owner a review path when a books gate's approvals leg is absent-or-stale.

memory_candidates.content: In this orchestrator design, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's verdict derivation is a fixed status-string lookup with zero access to a dispatch's raw command output; user_decision is explicitly producer-owned by the dispatched agent (set on .return-meta.json/handoff), and postflight only ever relays it verbatim into verdict=ask_user by field presence, never originating or reinterpreting it. When designing a new 'detect X and offer a choice' feature, the detection logic belongs in the agent that has the raw signal, never in postflight -- postflight structurally cannot classify what it never receives.

push-consent-relay.md's 'YES mints nothing' pattern (agent emits a user_decision; a human answer only tells the human the exact command to type themselves in a later, separate turn; the actual sensitive action is never auto-invoked from inside the autonomous dispatch) generalizes to any case where a dispatched subagent's sanctioned endpoint requires a tool/command unreachable from dispatch (e.g. AskUserQuestion-gated commands like skill-approve). Reuse this exact hand-off shape rather than inventing a feature-specific variant whenever a dispatched agent needs to request a human-only follow-up action.

In agent-system's books extension, no current books agent (plain or hard, research or implementation) invokes the fail-closed full-gate.sh/check.sh pipeline; books-gate.sh (the advisory --gate tier) covers only layer-lint + a Books.Meta closure check, and Stage 5's fixed verification runs lake build, books-tool validate/check, and the certifier's --check -- never the per-component full-gate.sh that would surface a check-approvals.sh-class failure. Any task needing to react to that gate's output must add a cross-cutting rule, since there is no fixed hook today; the gate is plan-directed, not automatic.
